text.p: Bank Hapoalim's securities department said Elite Industries Ltd's true value was $220 million to $240 million, against its current market value of $195 million.

It forecast earnings per share would be 0.85 shekels in 1996 and 0.95 in 1997 against a loss of 0.14 in 1995. Sales, however, will fall to 1.94 billion shekels in 1996 from 2.35 billion in 1995 and recover somewhat in 1997 to 2.0 billion as the company reduces operations in Western Europe.
Hapoalim said the Israeli food company would concentrate overseas activities in Eastern Europe, specifically Poland and Romania, except for a confectionery operation in France.
"In the long term we expect that like its competitors in the sector Elite will bring in a foreign food company as a strategic partner in order to face growing competition," Hapoalim said in a report.
Hapoalim also expects Elite to report capital gains in 1998-1999 from the sale of real estate in Israel valued on its books at $300,000 but which is really worth over $50 million.
